$comment: Publications, not products. What each outlet actually publishes, so we can weight and cite them. Never merged into bag records.

strategist-carryon.title: The Very Best Carry-on Luggage
strategist-carryon.author: Katherine Gillespie
strategist-carryon.size_baseline_note: US domestic standard. All picks assumed compliant, so the article compares capacity and weight instead of dimensions.
strategist-carryon.method: Editorial + reader reporting. No stated physical test protocol.

tl-carryon.title: The Best Carry-On Luggage of 2026
tl-carryon.author: Jasmine Grant
tl-carryon.size_baseline_note: No size filter. Several picks exceed the US standard (Samsonite Freeform 23x15x10).
tl-carryon.method: Pack test with a stated 4-day load; maneuverability over carpet/concrete; overhead-bin fit on a plane set; baseball bat and table drop; 6-month long-term.
self_inconsistent: 621 carry-ons tested in the intro vs 'over 650' in the methodology section

tl-international.title: The 14 Best International Carry-ons of 2026
tl-international.author: Asia London Palomba
tl-international.size_baseline_note: Stated as 'the most common international-carrier limit'. It is the US domestic standard. The article's own FAQ contradicts this, noting international is often smaller, 'sometimes under 21.7 in tall including handle and wheels'.
tl-international.method: Same T+L protocol: pack, roll over gravel/carpet/stone, drop and bat, overhead-bin fit, 6-month long-term.
self_inconsistent: 600+ bags in the intro vs 270 carry-ons in the methodology
Tumi headed '19 Degree Lite', called '10 Degree Lite International' in the body
Bagsmart listed at $110, prose says 'coming in at $150'
Bagsmart is Best value here, a runner-up in tl-carryon

packhacker-international.title: The Best Luggage for International Travel
packhacker-international.author: Eric Hergenreder
packhacker-international.size_baseline_note: The ROUNDUP prints no dimensions. The per-product review pages print dimensions, weight, capacity, AND a carry-on compliance percentage against 146 airlines. The roundup is a summary; the review page is the primary source.
packhacker-international.method: Weighted rolling test over smooth surface, brick/cobblestone, and grass. Method stated, raw per-surface ratings not published.
packhacker-international.handoff_quote: Sometimes, bag manufacturers make bags that are meant to be used as a carry on but are slightly too large to be used with some airlines. We recommend checking your specific airline before flying.
packhacker-international.beat: Primarily travel backpacks and one-bag travel. Wheeled luggage is secondary coverage — judging them as a luggage-sizing outlet on one roller roundup was the wrong test.

carry_on_compliance_feature.their_disclaimer: We take the measurements of the bag provided by the manufacturer and compare them to the allowance listed on airline websites. This should be used as a guideline rather than a rule. Bags can change size as you pack them out, and every airline's interpretation of compliance is different.
carry_on_compliance_feature.why_it_matters: This is our product, at greater carrier coverage, built on the one input our entire thesis says is wrong.

ricksteves-store.title: Carry-on Luggage
ricksteves-store.author: Rick Steves' Europe, Inc.
ricksteves-store.why_it_matters: The only source in this project - reviewer or manufacturer - that publishes the packing dimension AND the with-wheels dimension as separate figures. That distinction is our entire thesis, printed by a manufacturer on its own product page.
ricksteves-store.beat: Bags designed for European travel, sold direct. Barely covered by the US review circuit, which is why they appear in none of the four roundups.
ricksteves-store.caution: Still a manufacturer and still self-reported. The with-wheels figure is a claim to verify, not a measurement to adopt. Its value is that publishing both numbers makes the claim falsifiable in a way a single spec number never is.
self_inconsistent: Collection page meta says the bags are 'designed to fit in standard US airline bins'; the Rolling Carry-On product page says 'Fits European overhead bins with room to spare'.

travelpro-store.title: Maxlite 5 carry-on range
travelpro-store.author: Travelpro
travelpro-store.why_it_matters: The second manufacturer publishing both figures - and the only source anywhere that explains WHY it matters, in its own FAQ.
travelpro-store.thesis_quote: We publish both numbers. The case dimensions (the packing body only) are 19 x 15 x 7.75 in. The overall dimensions, which include wheels and carry handles, are 21.75 x 15.75 x 7.75 in. When airlines publish size limits they mean the overall size, so compare the overall number to your airline's limit.
travelpro-store.also_publishes: A per-airline carry-on size guide at /pages/airline-guides, and a regional-jet gate-check warning.
travelpro-store.caution: Tier 3 and self-reported. They also state the range is 'sizer-bin tested' on major US carriers, which is a testing claim we cannot verify.
